How do I know that my Linux is still secure?
How do you know any scanning tools you find are safe and not compromised?
You are the security, not the computer. The more you learn, the better you'll get at being secure.

A lot of these comments are not very useful. While they are correct in saying you never really know, you can get some things that might make you feel more comfort.

First, stay up-to-date on security updates. One big thing I'd recommend is using PfSense as your router software. There's all kinds of neat security tools that you can use with it. You could look at your network logs on your linux OS and your PfSense router to see if they match up.

 

There's also this AV scanner for linux:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clam_AntiVirus
AV scanners a great! They have access to everything as root, and cause irregular high system loads. Plus they need internet access for updates. What more could you ask for in a backdoor?

Are you talking about your home computer or a server? Either way you can try running Metasploit from another computer to its IP address https://www.metasploit.com/ There are live distributions that come with it pre-installed alongside hundreds of other useful security packages / audit tools https://www.kali.org/

Besides that the best person to know f your computer is infected is you. Is your computer behaving weirdly? Do you notice slowdowns or weird internet traffic, files on your hard disk, unknown processes using your CPU, user accounts you don't recognize, root or user accounts logged in that shouldn't be, etc? You can use typical sys admin tools to determine what is going on, set up proper permissions, etc to make sure your system is OK. Sure some things you can't notice but any virus/botnet malware is going to be using your computer for something worthwhile, like sending spam email or things like that. For example: if an hypothetical hacker is downloading all of your files that should be something you could notice even without tools just by internet lag.

I'm kinda ashamed of v/linux by seeing how much effort was put into worthless answers here. I hope even myself being pretty much ignorant could help you more than that. You probably should be searching the web for articles instead, as you can see there's not much to be found here.

The only good advice is the one that said: "how can I know I'm a 100% safe? well you can't". If something is really sensitive keep it on an external HD, offline and plug it only as needed. If you're doing something online and want to leave no tracks use Tails (or similar) instead on a live install https://tails.boum.org/ If security is a major concern make sure you're using the best secure Linux distro you can find and learn all you can about it, talk to other users online, etc.

Finally: the vast majority of viruses are targeted at Windows users because they make up the vast majority of the computers online. Even Mac computers double the number of Linux machines for personal use. Unless you're running a very outdated or insecure distribution or unless you have made yourself a target in particular for any reason or ran unknown binary code / installed unknown packages, chance are you're pretty safe. But I'm no expert...

http://tldp.org/HOWTO/Security-Quickstart-HOWTO/intrusion.html#HACKED

There are also tools like chkrootkit and rkhunter.

The whole field is called intrusion detection, and certainly worth learning about.
